attributes.names: Camfranglais (from camerounais, français and anglais), also called Francanglais.
attributes.description: A highly mixed urban youth speech made of Cameroonian French, Cameroonian English and Cameroon Pidgin English, with words from indigenous languages.
attributes.where: Mainly the big cities of Yaoundé and Douala.
attributes.speakers: Mostly young people aged 12 to 26, and mostly male, though more young women are using it.
attributes.writing: Written Camfranglais shows a strong tendency to make words from Duala, Ewondo, Basaa and Mokpe look French.
attributes.purpose: A way for youth to form a modern urban identity separate from French, English and indigenous languages.
attributes.concerns: Some educators worry it may hinder learning of standard French and English.
attributes.codes: It has no ISO 639-3 code. Glottolog uses camf1234.
